I am a woman farming here in Amhara, and this small maize plot is important for feeding my family. I will try to get some DAP and urea from the cooperative like last year, though sometimes it comes late. I keep a few animals, so I spread their manure on this plot before ploughing — it helps the soil. I use the seed I saved from last harvest because improved seed is expensive and not always available at our kebele; I do not have money for pesticides or irrigation, so I rely on the meher rains and my own hands, with help from my children when school allows.
